transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Um, I guess what really brought me in is that my mind just won’t stay on one thing anymore. 

It's getting to be a problem at work. I make jewelry, and lately when I'm at the bench, I just... I jump from checking a customer email to looking at a saw mark on a piece of metal, to some random noise outside. And then I look down and realize I’ve completely lost the whole work order I was supposed to be doing. I just can't seem to keep my focus on anything right now.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Yeah, I have. Um, especially these past couple weeks. I just... I wake up with this really heavy, hollow feeling. It's hard to explain, but it's like the shine has just gone out of everything, you know? There have even been a few mornings where I've just sat in my truck and cried before going in to open the shop.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

I don't think so, no. I mean, I still like making jewelry when I can actually focus on it, and I still like hanging out with my friends. It's just that heavy feeling I mentioned, but I wouldn't say I've lost interest in the stuff I usually like to do.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually energetic or wired and needed much less sleep than usual?

Yeah, actually. There was a while where I was sleeping maybe two or three hours a night. But I wasn't tired. I'd get up completely clear-headed and just... really excited to start cutting stones or posting new designs online way before sunrise. It felt like I just didn't need the rest.
During that time when you were sleeping only two or three hours, did you also feel unusually euphoric or on top of the world?

Yeah, I did. Like, after this one craft show, I felt completely lit up, you know? Just... larger than life one minute. But then, if anyone tried to tell me to slow down or stick to my normal shop hours, I'd just snap at them. I got really irritable if people got in my way.
During that unusually energized time, were you ever hospitalized because of it?
No, I wasn't. I mean, I know I was acting pretty intense and getting on people's nerves, but it never got to the point where I had to go to a hospital or anything like that.
About that time when you only slept two or three hours a night and still felt energized, how many days in a row did that last?
I'd say it was about two weeks. That whole wired, kind of out-of-control stretch started right after I got an award at a jewelry show, and it just went on like that for about two weeks straight.
During that two-week energized period, did it cause serious problems in your life or work?

Yeah, it did. I mean... I missed a major custom delivery for a client, which is really bad for business. And my shop records just got completely disorganized. It got so messy that I actually had to stop taking on any new work for now just to try and sort it out. Plus, my family has been checking in on me a lot more lately. They got pretty worried about how far I'd slipped from my usual routines.
During that energized two-week period, did you have any experiences like hearing voices or becoming convinced of something that other people said wasn’t true?
No, I didn't have anything like that happen. I didn't hear any voices or... believe anything weird. I was just really wired and moving too fast, but I was still, you know, living in reality.
Before age 12, did you often have trouble paying attention or staying organized?
No, not really. I mean, I did fine in school and I don't remember having any major issues with paying attention or keeping my things organized back then. I was just a regular kid.
